newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Thursday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose slightly to 1.877 billion yuan from 1.7 billion yuan with the seven-day contract the most active.
Traders said news that the local currency interbank market had admitted seven foreign banks as second-tier members did not move the interbank rates on Thursday.
"This is relatively positive news because the admission of foreign banks will add liquidity to the market," one trader said.
"Some non-banking financial centers are encouraged by the rising (domestic) A share markets and were the most active traders on Thursday," said a second trader.

Under the new arrangement, the foreign banks admitted to the interbank market are allowed to borrow and lend short-term money through the short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the People's Bank, the central bank.

The market now has 20 major state banks' head offices and 35 short-term financial centres as first-tier members. Hundreds of other banks, major state bank branches and brokerages are second-tier members trading through the centres.
